title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is an elementary scratch page about finite symmetry groups generated by reflections and rotations. It fits the 'Teichmülleries' setting: the extended (orientation-reversing) modular or mapping-class groups and the cartographic groups.

(1) Top left. The presentation sigma_1^2 = sigma_2^2 = (sigma_1 sigma_2)^2 = 1 is a Klein four-group generated by two commuting involutions. Rotations rho_1, rho_2 are added, related by sigma_1 rho_1 = rho_2^{-1}. This is the usual pattern of reflection groups, where a reflection conjugates one rotation to the inverse of another. It resembles Grothendieck's cartographic groups <sigma_0, sigma_1, sigma_2> and their oriented subgroups generated by rotations rho_i.

(2) Then come lifted relations tau~ rho~ = rho~^{-1}, tau~ sigma~ = sigma~^{-1}, and rho~^3. These give an outer involution tau inverting an order-3 generator rho and an order-2 (or 4) generator sigma. This is the standard way to pass from PSL_2(Z) = Z/2 * Z/3 (or SL_2(Z)) to PGL_2(Z) (or GL_2(Z)) by adjoining an orientation-reversing element. The matrices at the bottom, (1 1; 0 1) and (1 -1; 0 1), are a translation and its inverse. Conjugation by diag(1,-1) inverts T, consistent with this reading.

(3) Figures. A tube or torus with a basis e_1, e_2 and loops around it suggests a lattice or torus with its two generating cycles. A stack of cubes with a cylinder on top and axes x, y comes with the map x -> -x, y -> y, i.e. a reflection. A prism with labelled vertices a_i, b_i, c_i (i = 0..3) looks like a cell decomposition of a fundamental domain, with arrows indicating edge identifications.

(4) Main computation, right and bottom. On C x R (z complex, t real) define
- sigma(z,t) = (iz, -t),
- sigma_1(z,t) = (z-bar, t),
- sigma_2(z,t) = (-z-bar, t).
Then:
- sigma^2(z,t) = (-z, t) = sigma_1 sigma_2 = sigma_2 sigma_1.
- sigma^4 = 1 and sigma_1^2 = sigma_2^2 = 1.
- sigma_2 = sigma_1 sigma^2 = sigma^2 sigma_1.
- The chain (z,t) -> (z-bar, t) -> (i z-bar, -t) -> (-iz, -t) verifies sigma_1 sigma sigma_1 = sigma^{-1}.

So <sigma, sigma_1> is the dihedral group D_4 of order 8. Its center is <sigma^2>, with sigma^2 = sigma_1 sigma_2. It is the full symmetry group of the square lattice Z[i] (automorphisms of the elliptic curve with j = 1728, including antiholomorphic ones). Modulo the center sigma^2 = -1 one recovers the Klein four-group of the first line. That is the stabiliser of tau = i in PGL_2(Z), where sigma_1, sigma_2 are the two real structures and sigma acts as -1 on a transversal real parameter t.

The page thus checks how the Klein-four relation in PGL_2(Z) lifts to a dihedral group of order 8 in GL_2(Z). The crossed-out '(sigma_1, sigma_2)', '(sigma_1 sigma_2)^2' and 'D_sigma' mark Grothendieck correcting himself: in the lift, (sigma_1 sigma_2)^2 is no longer automatically trivial, and sigma_1 sigma_2 = sigma^2. This is local analysis at the elliptic point of order 2 (or 4 in SL_2) of the extended modular group, relevant to real/anti-holomorphic structure on the moduli of genus-1 curves.
errors: No mathematical errors found. The '?' after sigma_2(sigma) = sigma^{-1} is resolved on the page itself: sigma_2 = sigma_1 sigma^2, and sigma^2 commutes with sigma, so sigma_2 also inverts sigma.
The relation sigma_1 rho_1 = rho_2^{-1} in the top block is stated without the defining context for rho_1, rho_2, so it cannot be checked independently.

ideas.what: Dihedral group of order 8 generated by z -> iz (with t -> -t) and complex conjugation; sigma^2 = sigma_1 sigma_2 central; lifting the Klein four-group relations
ideas.modern_name: Automorphism group of the square lattice / stabiliser of i in GL_2(Z), central extension of the Klein four-group by Z/2
ideas.where_published: Related material appears in Esquisse d'un programme (cartographic groups, PGL_2(Z)), but not this computation explicitly

ideas.what: Adjoining an involution tau inverting rho (order 3) and sigma to pass from PSL_2(Z) to PGL_2(Z)
ideas.modern_name: Extended modular group PGL_2(Z) as a semidirect product / amalgam of dihedral groups D_2 *_{Z/2} D_3
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses cartographic groups and PSL_2(Z)/PGL_2(Z) in passing

ideas.what: Reflection presentation sigma_1^2 = sigma_2^2 = (sigma_1 sigma_2)^2 = 1 with rotations rho_i = products of reflections
ideas.modern_name: Cartographic group / Coxeter-type presentation of map symmetry groups
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme, sections on dessins and cartographic groups

deep.surprise_reason: The page holds routine verifications of dihedral and modular-group relations, plus sketches of tori and cell complexes. It is an elementary working check, with nothing absent from the standard literature.
transcription_corrections: Line 3 reads 'sigma_1 rho_1 = rho_2^{-1}'; the subscript on rho after sigma_1 is hastily written but plausibly 1.
The fragment '(x,y,z) -> ix,' is incomplete in the original; it is probably an abandoned first attempt at the formula (z,t) -> (iz,-t) written below it.
The '?' after sigma_2(sigma) = sigma^{-1} belongs to that line; it marks doubt, not a missing formula.
The struck-out symbol before 'D_sigma' is illegible.
